newsitem.title: UK: Reed Elsevier growth seen in single figures.
newsitem.headline: Reed Elsevier growth seen in single figures.

text.p: The strength of sterling is likely to keep earnings growth from Anglo-Dutch publisher Reed Elsevier Plc in single figures this year, analysts said on Wednesday.
Reed Elsevier co-chairman Nigel Stapleton said that the current strength of the British currency, if maintained, could depress headline earnings by a factor of five percent this year.

"Reed can produce 10 or 11 percent earnings growth on flat currencies without acquisitions," said Louise Barton of Henderson Crosthwaite. "Currencies may bring that back to nearer five or six percent this year," she added.
Henderson is forecasting 1997 headline earnings of 865 million pounds, an increase from 805 million last year.
That view was echoed by Colin Tennant of UBS, which has a 1997 pre-tax forecast of 870 million pounds.
"General trading seems to be good and currency is the reason why earnings growth is likely to be in single digits," he said.
Analysts said that the likely currency impact had largely been anticipated and that the underlying performance from Reed was impressive.
They noted that organic revenue growth at six percent was the highest for several years and that overall operating margins improved by 2.6 percentage points to 25.3 percent.

Reed management told analysts in London that the company planned to invest some 60-65 million pounds on developing new electronic information products this year. The company said this may constrain historical rates of margin improvement.
Reed shares slipped 25p to 1148.4p by 1440 GMT but analysts said this must be viewed in the light of a rise of well over 10 percent in recent weeks.
"A lot of the recent rise has been built on some very flimsy speculation," said one analyst.
